title: State Cyber Crime Cell v. AlphaTech Labs (Defense Algorithm Exfiltration Case)
citation: Independent Contributor: Cyber Law & Digital Forensics Clinic (Case #BLIND-2024-F02)
confidence_note: High - Corroborated network telemetry and physical airport alibi vs planted USB

ground_truth.culprit_summary: Foreign APT Group (Remotely compromised workstation via spear-phishing)
ground_truth.rationale: Network firewall logs show C2 beaconing and memory injection mimicking user credentials. Workstation owner was physically in transit on commercial flight during the 02:14 AM exfiltration window.

hypotheses.label: Senior Firmware Architect Neil K.
hypotheses.statement: Architect downloaded proprietary drone telemetry code onto personal USB to transfer to foreign competitor.

hypotheses.label: Foreign Advanced Persistent Threat (APT Group)
hypotheses.statement: Foreign cyber-espionage syndicate remotely compromised internal subnet via weaponized PDF backdoor and exfiltrated code using architect's cached credentials.

hypotheses.label: IT Infrastructure Admin Vikram D.
hypotheses.statement: Disgruntled system administrator used domain controller root privilege to exfiltrate code and deliberately frame Neil K.

exhibits.name: Network Perimeter Firewall & Endpoint EDR Forensic Dump
exhibits.text: EDR memory forensic extraction reveals Neil K.'s workstation process svchost.exe was injected with a Cobalt Strike beacon payload at 02:08 AM. 4.2 GB of encrypted git archive packets were transmitted to an offshore command-and-control server in Frankfurt. The process initiated automatically via a task scheduler backdoor planted 5 days prior via a malicious PDF email attachment.

exhibits.name: Bangalore International Airport CISF Gate Log & Flight Manifest
exhibits.text: CISF biometric e-gate logs and IndiGo Airlines flight 6E-512 manifest establish Neil K. passed through security at Bangalore Airport at 01:15 AM and was airborne between 01:55 AM and 04:30 AM without in-flight Wi-Fi connectivity, conclusively disproving physical access to his workstation at the time of exfiltration.

exhibits.name: SanDisk Flash Drive Found in Neil K. Office Desk
exhibits.text: A 64GB SanDisk USB recovered from Neil K.'s desk drawer contained compiled software binaries. Forensic file metadata analysis demonstrates last written timestamp was 7 months prior to the incident; zero files from the compromised drone guidance repository were present on the media.

exhibits.name: Git Repository Access Audit Log
exhibits.text: Git enterprise server logs indicate the repository was pulled using SSH key neil_rsa_pub. While initially casting circumstantial suspicion on Neil, cryptographic analysis shows the private key was stored unencrypted on his compromised workstation disk and harvested by the malware.

adversarial_exhibit.name: Planted Resignation Resentment Memo
adversarial_exhibit.text: Unverified draft email stating 'I will take the guidance code with me if compensation is not matched.'
